goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:10 — Updating a nonexistent embeddable-host dereferences nil and returns a 500 instead of the resource API's expected 404.
app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:15 — Deleting a nonexistent embeddable-host dereferences nil and returns a 500 instead of the resource API's expected 404.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb, the destroy method does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` followed by `host.destroy`. If no record exists with that id, `where(...).first` returns nil, and calling `nil.destroy` will raise a NoMethodError, resulting in a 500 error instead of a proper 404. This is a real bug - the code doesn't handle the case where the host doesn't exist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Migrated host values keep legacy schemes/paths, but runtime lookup compares only URI.host, so those formerly allowed entries are rejected after migration.

adjudication.rationale: The migration at line 25 inserts host values directly from the old site_settings without stripping schemes or paths: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. However, the new EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback strips 'http://' and 'https://' prefixes and paths, and the host_allowed? method uses URI(host).host for comparison. This means if the old embeddable_hosts setting contained entries like 'http://example.com' or 'https://example.com/path', they would be migrated as-is but the runtime lookup would fail to match them because it compares against URI.host (just 'example.com'). The migration should have applied the same normalization that the model applies.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — A configured embed category whose category has been deleted makes the empty query result indexed as a row and aborts the migration.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the migration code at line 11: `category_id = execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. If the embed_category setting references a category that has been deleted, the query returns no rows. Accessing `[0]` on an empty result would return nil, and calling `['id']` on nil would raise a NoMethodError, causing the migration to abort. The code does handle the case where category_id is 0 (falls back to uncategorized), but it doesn't handle the case where the query returns no rows at all.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — The backfill stores legacy URL-form hosts verbatim, so entries such as https://example.com no longer match URI host lookups after migration.

adjudication.rationale: The migration at line 25 executes `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` where `h` comes directly from the old `embeddable_hosts` setting which could contain URLs like 'https://example.com'. The new EmbeddableHost model has a `before_validation` callback that strips 'http://' and 'https://' prefixes, but this callback is NOT invoked during the raw SQL INSERT in the migration. Meanwhile, the `host_allowed?` method in EmbeddableHost does `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` comparing against `uri.host` (just the hostname). So if the old setting had 'https://example.com', it gets stored as 'https://example.com' in the database, but lookups compare against 'example.com', causing a mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:31 — The irreversible deletion of the two source settings prevents rollback from restoring the migrated configuration.

adjudication.rationale: The migration at db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb line 31 executes `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')` which permanently removes the original settings after migrating them to the new embeddable_hosts table. This is a one-way migration with no `down` method defined, meaning if the migration needs to be rolled back, the original configuration data would be lost. This is a legitimate architectural concern about data migration reversibility, though it's a design choice rather than a bug - the migration intentionally converts the data format.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Interpolating legacy host values into SQL makes an apostrophe-containing setting abort the migration instead of safely backfilling it.

adjudication.rationale: The migration at line 25 uses string interpolation to insert host values directly into SQL: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. If any host value contains an apostrophe (single quote), it would break the SQL syntax and cause the migration to fail. This is a real SQL injection/escaping bug that could cause data migration failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — Each embed authorization performs an unindexed case-insensitive host lookup, causing a full table scan as configured hosts grow.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the `record_for_host` method in `app/models/embeddable_host.rb` performs a `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` query without an index. This is a valid performance concern - as the number of embeddable hosts grows, this will result in a full table scan. However, this is not a bug (the code works correctly), but rather a performance/scalability concern. The diff shows this is new code being added, and the table is expected to be small (admin-configured hosts), so while it's a legitimate architectural concern, it's not critical. A reasonable reviewer might suggest adding an index on `lower(host)` for better performance.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:9 — The migration dereferences the first category-query row even when no configured embed category exists, aborting upgrades with a nil error.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the migration code in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, lines 9-14 show: `category_id = execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. If no embed_category setting exists or no matching category is found, the query returns an empty result set, and accessing `[0]['id']` on an empty result will cause a nil error. The code does have a fallback check `if category_id == 0` on line 17, but this won't be reached if the initial query result is empty/nil because the error occurs before that check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:10 — Updating or deleting a host removed concurrently (or requested with an invalid ID) dereferences nil and returns a 500 instead of a handled not-found response.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb, the update and destroy methods use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` which returns nil if no record is found. In the update method, `save_host(host)` is called with a potentially nil host, and in destroy, `host.destroy` is called on a potentially nil host. Neither method checks if the host exists before operating on it, which would cause a NoMethodError (500 error) instead of a proper 404 response when the record doesn't exist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:46 — Failed host deletions have no rejection handler, leaving an unhandled request failure with no user-visible error.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 46 in app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6, the delete action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...)` but there is no `.catch()` handler for the promise. If the destroyRecord() call fails (e.g., network error, server error), the promise rejection will be unhandled and the user will not see any error message. This contrasts with the save() action on line 37 which properly includes `.catch(popupAjaxError)` to handle failures. This is a real defect - failed deletions will silently fail with no user feedback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:5 — The new controller spec only asserts inheritance and never exercises host create/update/destroy or category persistence.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new spec file at spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb only contains a single test asserting that the controller inherits from AdminController. The diff shows the controller (app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb) has create, update, and destroy actions with actual business logic (saving hosts with category_id, validation, etc.), but none of this functionality is tested. This is a legitimate concern about missing test coverage for newly added nontrivial logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:36 — No test verifies that importing an embed selects and assigns the matched host's category.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there's no test verifying that importing an embed assigns the matched host's category. However, looking at spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb in the diff, there IS a test that verifies this: the test creates an embeddable_host fabricator, imports content, and then explicitly asserts 'expect(post.topic.category).to eq(embeddable_host.category)' on line 37. This directly tests the category assignment functionality.
